messages:
ashley (oncall): :rotating_light: PAGED: multiple decode workers in 'stream-decode-prod' hitting GPU OOMs + container restarts. Customer-facing errors and ~6% request drop rate on streaming paths. stack: decode/streaming path. root ts 5890012345
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-589001 — streaming decode OOM spike. Pager escalated to oncall. Slack thread pinned.
ashley (oncall): quick snapshot — node pool 'g4-decode-12' showing 3/8 nodes with repeated CUDA exceptions and kube restarts. errors look like runaway generation from some client sessions (max_tokens header mismatch seen in traces).
mike (eng-runtime): grabbing GPU logs now. seeing repeated: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in decode loop, then container exit 137. Also large KV cache growth on a few sessions.
priya (sre): oncall, do we have a quarantine for offending sessions? can we circuit-break at the LB for streaming route?
ashley (oncall): not yet. planning: 1) throttle streaming route to 50% concurrency 2) route heavy requests to smaller model variant 3) evict problematic pods 4) customer update. anyone object?
sam (infra): I can apply a temporary rate-limit at gateway. patching nginx route `streaming-v1` -> add `limit_req zone=streaming burst=200 nodelay;` pushing in 30s.
mike (eng-runtime): also recommend enabling prefix-KV eviction for long sessions: toggling `kv_cache.max_items=5000` on the running model config. That will drop very long contexts.
kevin (support): which customers impacted? I have a ticket from AcmeCorp complaining about dropped streams and 502s. We should send a short status. draft: "We're aware of intermittent streaming failures, implementing throttles and fallbacks; expect <15m to stabilize." OK?
jordan (oncall-next): taking handoff in 15. if you need me earlier ping @jordan.
ashley (oncall): sam pushed gateway limit, confirmed `limit_req` in place. observed immediate drop in concurrent inflight streams from 820 -> 420. request drop rate trending down.
priya (sre): good. initiate rolling eviction of the 3 bad nodes so Kubernetes reschedules them onto healthy hosts. use `kubectl drain` with `--force --delete-local-data` to kick pods off.
sam (infra): running command: ```bash
kubectl drain g4-decode-12-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl delete pod -l app=stream-decode -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=g4-decode-12-node-3
```
kevin (support): customer update ready. Sending now: "We have throttled streaming traffic and are routing heavy generation to a fallback model. We're actively evicting affected nodes and expect service to stabilize in ~10-20 minutes. Apologies for the disruption." :memo:
mike (eng-runtime): while nodes restart, enable fallback routing policy to model-compact-v2 for streaming heavy requests. set policy weight: compact=100 for route `streaming-fallback` until further notice. This reduces GPU pressure.
ashley (oncall): applied routing override to force fallback, confirmed in control plane. telemetry shows per-token GPU usage down ~40%.
priya (sre): watch for regressions — if error rate drops below 1% keep fallback. if still high, we'll consider autoscaling additional decode pools or enabling JS-side token caps.
jordan (oncall-next): I'm up now, taking the incident. ashley — handing off context: paged for CUDA OOMs on decode; mitigations applied: gateway throttle, kv eviction, routing to compact model, node drain. I'll coordinate customer follow-up and postmortem.
ashley (oncall): thanks — logging actions to INC-589001. will add detailed commands and timeline to the incident ticket.
srebot: Note: created temporary SLO override for streaming route to avoid noisy alerts while we stabilize.
mike (eng-runtime): one more note — logs show a small percentage of requests with `max_tokens` header ~= 100000 (likely client bug). we've added a guard in the router to cap `max_tokens` to 10000 for streaming routes. patch applied.
kevin (support): copying final customer note: "Root cause appears to be a combination of runaway client-specified max_tokens and long KV caches. We've applied request caps and fallbacks; please reopen if you see more drops." sending to affected customers list.
jordan (oncall-next): marking handoff complete. last metrics check: request drop rate down to 0.9%, error 500s down to baseline. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then close.
ashley (oncall): closing thread here, will attach logs and remediation steps to the incident doc. thanks all. :thumbsup:"
